characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Field-emission scanning electron microscope (FE-SEM CZ/MIRA I LMH, TESCAN, Czech) equipped with an EBSD detector (Hikari, AMETEK EDAX, U.S.A) using a step size of 200 nm
characterization_methods.key_findings: Triplex ferrite + martensite + austenite; large interconnected yellow/orange (martensite) banded regions with red austenite in a dominant green ferrite matrix; banding is less frequent and more homogeneously distributed than at 500 °C, and no deformation bands were observed at 600 °C.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Phase map (PM) overlaid on image quality (IQ) map, 20 µm scale bar; compression axis (CA) indicated
characterization_methods.purpose: To identify the phase constitution and strain distribution of the microstructure after compression at 600 °C to true strain 0.6

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Gotech AI-7000 universal testing machine equipped with a programmable furnace
characterization_methods.key_findings: 600 °C flow curve plateaus around 400 MPa; significant drop in stress level when temperature increases from 500 to 600 °C; appreciable flow softening after true strain 0.3 at 500–600 °C.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 600 °C, strain rate 0.001 s^-1, up to true strain 0.6; soaked 5 min before testing; immediately water quenched
characterization_methods.purpose: To obtain the compressive flow curve and extracted stress levels vs temperature for the material

analytical_models.equation_role: Interpretation of phase stability and the driving force for bidirectional ferrite↔austenite transformation
analytical_models.model_name: Gibbs free energy / modified Gibbs energy model
analytical_models.model_note: Point A marks the composition at which BCC (ferrite) and FCC (austenite) possess the same Gibbs free energy, making co-occurrence / simultaneous bidirectional transformation probable; Mn partitioning mainly dictates the Gibbs free energy and phase stability, whereas Al variation has little remarkable influence. Applied to the alloy system; isothermal sections shown at 500 and 550 °C.

parameters.name: Point A (BCC/FCC equal Gibbs energy composition)
Equilibrium Gibbs energy at point A (Mn, 500 °C)

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Equilibrium calculations for the Fe-11.15Mn-5.6Al-0.07C (wt.%) system: mass percent of Mn and Al in each constituent phase vs temperature (0–1600 °C), and Gibbs free energy of BCC and FCC vs %Mn and %Al at isothermal sections of 500 and 550 °C; nominal composition line marked at ~11 %Mn.
computational_details.simulation_method: CALPHAD thermodynamic calculation using the Gibbs free energy model (equilibrium phase and energy calculations)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Predicted elemental partitioning (Mn into austenite, Al into ferrite) and the resulting equal Gibbs energies of ferrite and austenite were consistent with the SEM-measured partitioning of the deformed steel (Table 1, 500 °C condition).

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Occurrence of deformation bands and deformation-induced bidirectional ferrite↔austenite transformation, and homogeneity of strain distribution
comparative_performance.note: At 600 °C the frequently distributed deformation bands and the simultaneous deformation-induced ferrite to austenite / austenite to ferrite transformations observed at 500 °C could NOT be characterized; strain distribution is more homogeneous at 600 °C due to the higher capability for strain distribution at higher temperature.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: ESR-received material was homogenized at 1200 °C for 1 h to eliminate any probable segregation.
Hot rolled through 5 passes in the temperature range 1100–1200 °C, followed by air quenching.
Annealed at 950 °C for 1 h to attain a triplex (ferrite + austenite + martensite) microstructure; this is the parent state (proc_annealed-950c-1h) of the sample.
Compression specimens were soaked at the deformation temperature for 5 min before testing to reach thermal equilibrium.
High temperature compression test carried out on a Gotech AI-7000 universal testing machine under a strain rate of 0.001 s^-1 up to a true strain of 0.6.
Specimens were immediately water quenched after compression to preserve the deformed microstructure at high temperature.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: compression specimen soaked 5 min at temperature, immediately water quenched after testing

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Compressive true stress–strain curve at 600 °C rises to ~400 MPa and stays nearly flat (plateau); appreciable flow softening reported after a true strain of 0.3 in the 500–600 °C flow curves.

aliases: deformed at 600 °C down to true strain 0.6

defects.note: No deformation bands were observed at 600 °C (the frequently distributed deformation bands were only seen at 500 °C), attributed to the higher capability for strain distribution at higher temperature; banding is less frequent and more uniformly distributed than at 500 °C.

phases_present.morphology: red islands/bands within the ferrite matrix (FCC regions lying within the dominant BCC matrix)

phases_present.crystal_structure: BCC (thermally induced; both martensite and ferrite hold BCC structure)
phases_present.morphology: large interconnected yellow/orange banded regions within the green ferrite matrix

structures.overall_structure: Triplex ferrite + austenite + thermally induced martensite microstructure; after warm compression at 600 °C to a true strain of 0.6 the EBSD phase maps still resolve the three constituent phases, but strain distribution is more homogeneous, deformation bands are less frequently distributed than at 500 °C, and no deformation-induced bidirectional ferrite↔austenite transformation was characterized.

unmapped_findings: At the higher temperature of 600 °C, neither the frequently distributed deformation bands nor the simultaneous deformation-induced ferrite to austenite (DIAT) / austenite to ferrite (DIFT) transformations could be characterized in the deformed microstructure, in contrast to deformation at 500 °C (see Fig. 3e).

The 600 °C condition is the higher-temperature counterpart of the 500 °C/0.6 condition; strain distribution is more homogeneous at 600 °C owing to the higher capability for strain distribution at higher temperature.

The chemical composition (elemental partitioning) SEM analysis reported in Table 1 (Mn 10.3±0.1 / Al 6.0±0.1 wt.% in ferrite and Mn 12.8±0.1 / Al 4.7±0.1 wt.% in austenite) is explicitly stated to be for the specimen deformed at 500 °C, and therefore does not pertain to this 600 °C sample.
